sources.name: Printed cards
sources.origin: Physical cards. The origin of every scan and photo. For Western cards from Base Set to Platinum (1999–2010), and Japanese cards before 2006, no official digital image was ever published online, so every picture of those cards is somebody's scan or photo. The only official digital card images of that era we found are offline and small: Japan's 2005 Card Encyclopedia CD-ROM (162×226).

sources.origin: カードずかん & デッキビルダー, a Windows program on the CD-ROM of the Japanese Master Kit (2005). It holds every Japanese card released until then: 3,688 cards with name, reading, expansion, collection number, illustrator, promo source and holo flag, each with an official digital image. The images are clean print renders, not scans, but only 162×226. The only official digital images of Japanese 1996–2005 cards we found; too small to use as card images, but a complete official card list for that era.

sources.name: Pokémon Paradijs scans (Martin)

terms.summary: Martin's own scans; no licence published. pkmncards.com credits "Martin of Pokémon Paradijs" for most of its pre-HGSS images.

sources.origin: Martin of Pokémon Paradijs scanned almost the entire English vintage era (Base Set → Platinum) in consistent, high quality. Those scans are the backbone of English vintage images on the web: pkmncards, pokemontcg.io, Scrydex, TCGdex, TCGplayer and TCG Collector serve them. Remarkable work that deserves a credit wherever it's used. The original site, pokemon-paradijs.com, is preserved in the Wayback Machine (2014 crawl): 13,264 images in 183 set folders from Base Set to Plasma Freeze, with reverse-holo and 1st-edition variants, and Dutch Base Set, Jungle and Fossil. Compared file by file with TCGdex: its English e-card, EX, Diamond & Pearl, Platinum, POP and promo images are Martin's original pictures (3,806 files). For Base Set → Neo and EX Ruby & Sapphire, Sandstorm and Hidden Legends, TCGdex has different scans of the same cards (1,231); we can't tell whether those are later rescans by Martin or someone else's. 331 of Martin's scans are cards TCGdex lists without an image: trainer kits, Aquapolis and Skyridge holos, the Unown set, McDonald's 2011/2012, promos. pokemonkaart.nl's Dutch scans are pixel-identical to his, so the Dutch images are Martin's work as well.

sources.name: TCGdex

submissions.how: Images via the Ingest upload page (manager.tcgdex.net/ingest); card data via GitHub pull requests (CONTRIBUTING rejects AI-assisted data PRs)

terms.summary: Card data MIT-licensed. Image sources aren't listed per card. Takes image uploads through its Ingest page.

sources.origin: By pixel match: HGSS → Mega Evolution Pitch Black (me05) in every Western language is the exact same files as the game-client renders malie published (often months earlier). Pixels can't tell whether TCGdex took them from malie or from the game directly. The newest set, 30th Celebration (Sep 2026), is different: a differently cropped render that isn't malie's file and was online about 5 hours before malie's export, so it came from another source. English 1999–2010 is 94% the same files pokemontcg.io serves. Against Martin's own site (Wayback, 2014): e-card → Platinum, POP and promos are his original pictures (3,806 files, EX Dragon and EX FireRed & LeafGreen included); Base Set → Neo, EX Ruby & Sapphire, Sandstorm and Hidden Legends are different scans. French vintage: 43 of 96 sampled pre-HGSS images are the same files pkmcards.fr serves (from 0 of 10 in Base Set to 30 of 33 in the EX era), and 22 are pokemontcg.io's English files: 18 of 27 French POP-series images are the English scans. No German before HGSS. Sampled zh-cn images are the Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) print.

callouts.title: Korean: official images are watermarked
callouts.body: Pokémon Korea's official site (pokemoncard.co.kr) is the only digital source, and it serves only watermarked images. Every Korean fan database we found links to those same files. PriceCharting's Korean images are mostly photos of real cards (no watermark, but glare and texture), plus some official watermarked ones. No clean digital Korean image found anywhere (2010 → today).
callouts.short: The official site pokemoncard.co.kr serves only watermarked images, and the Korean fan databases we found link to those same files.

callouts.title: Simplified Chinese: the full set only at 300×419
callouts.body: The only complete official source is Pokémon Shanghai's WeChat mini-program. Its images were scraped into the GitHub dataset duanxr/PTCG-CHS-Datasets at the app's native 300×419. Larger official renders (868×1212 and up) exist only for the 20–30 cards each product page on pokemon.cn highlights; 52poke has collected 1,328 of them (≈ 15% of the cards). AREAZERO.GG (tcg.mik.moe) shows the same 300×419 images as the dataset (pixel-identical in our sample) and no extra cards in the sets we compared; TCG Collector and PriceCharting carry the same renders for the cards we sampled. The dataset forbids redistribution without Pokémon Shanghai's written consent. Sampled TCGdex zh-cn images are the Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) print.
callouts.short: The only complete set we found is the WeChat mini-program's, at 300×419; larger official renders exist for ≈ 15% of the cards.

badge.label: the full set we found is small

callouts.title: Better quality exists than TCGdex serves
callouts.body: TCGdex serves 600×825. malie's originals are 734×1024 with transparent corners; the Singapore English print on asia.pokemon-card.com is 744×1040; TCG Collector's Japanese scans reach 1280×1788; bisafans' German vintage photos are ≈ 860×1200; Poképédia's French vintage scans reach 1068 px wide; pokemon.cn's Simplified Chinese product renders are 868×1212 and up.
callouts.short: malie, the Singapore English print, TCG Collector, bisafans, Poképédia and pokemon.cn have larger originals than TCGdex's 600×825.

badge.label: largest originals we found; TCGdex serves 600 px

callouts.title: Western 1999–2010 has no official digital image
callouts.body: No Base Set → Platinum card was ever published as an official digital image online. Every image of those cards, TCGdex's included, is somebody's scan. For English, nearly everyone uses the scans by Martin of Pokémon Paradijs; TCGdex's e-card → Platinum images are his original files (3,806, checked against his archived site). Japanese 1996–2006 is the same story online: the largest clean sets of scans we found are TCG Collector's and pcg-search.com's. Offline, the 2005 Card Encyclopedia CD-ROM has an official image of every Japanese card up to 2005, but only at 162×226.
callouts.short: We found no Base Set → Platinum card published as an official digital image online; for English, nearly everyone uses the scans by Martin of Pokémon Paradijs.
